footer.about: Douglas Fry Roofing is a family roofing company in Wichita. Doug Fry started it in 1981, and his son Jason works beside him. We install and repair tile, DaVinci, Brava, wood shake, asphalt and standing seam metal roofs.
why: You speak with an owner, never a commissioned salesperson
Written estimates with scope, warranty and price

You have been roofing Wichita since 1981, and your customers say it better than any slogan could: "Very honest and friendly service." "Excellent on time service, informative, fair price, and knowledgeable." That is 4.8 stars on 79 Google reviews.
Your website shows none of it. On a phone it runs off the right edge of the screen, so the call buttons and most of the menu can't be seen.
So we built a site around what your customers already say, with tile, DaVinci and an owner on the phone at the front.
strategy.cardsHeading: Be the Roofing Company People Find on Google
strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page: what your site does today and what we changed.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: The page Google reads to learn who you are and where you work.
problems: The top of the page says only "Douglas Fry Roofing, Inc.", so Google can't tell you are a roofing company in Wichita.
On a phone the page runs off the right edge, and the "Get In Touch" call buttons sit off the screen.
None of your 4.8-star Google reviews appear on the site.
fixes: A headline that says roofing company in Wichita, KS, right at the top.
The page fits a phone, with both numbers one tap away.
Real customer reviews, each beside the point it proves.
cards.alsoAdd: Every page set up behind the scenes so Google and AI tools like ChatGPT know exactly what you do, where you work, and what your customers say.

cards.title: Roof Replacement
cards.why: The biggest job you do, and your tile, DaVinci and metal work is scattered across product pages.
problems: Replacement is spread over five product pages with no single page that says "roof replacement Wichita".
Nothing explains the written estimate or the insurance help your reviews praise.
fixes: One page for roof replacement in Wichita, KS: materials, hail claims, written estimate and warranty.
Reviews on tile, Brava and hail claims beside the work they describe.
cards.alsoAdd: Pages planned from what Google actually shows for each search, so every page targets something people really look for.

cards.title: Roof Repair
cards.why: Tile repair is what other roofers send people to you for.
problems: The "Repair Services" menu link opens a page whose address ends in "tile-roof-systems-copy".
Tile repair is covered on four pages, and two show raw photo file names like "IMG_0042.heic" as captions.
fixes: One roof repair page for Wichita, KS, covering tile, shake, asphalt, DaVinci and metal.
Clean captions, and tile repair reviews beside each repair.
cards.alsoAdd: A check of what your competitors offer, so services you didn’t think to mention still get their own pages.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: Where a customer with a leaking roof reaches you.
problems: The (316) 264-1511 number is plain text on every page and cannot be tapped.
The only form sits far down the homepage, and there is no email address anywhere.
fixes: Both numbers tap to call, with your address and a list of what to have ready.
cards.alsoAdd: Call and form tracking that shows which pages and towns your leads come from.

onboardingQuestions: What is (316) 264-1511 for (office, sales, an old line, a crew line)? It is shown as "Office" and second after (316) 655-9777. Should it be tap-to-call?
Years in business: the site says "Roofing Since 1981" but also "30-plus years" and "over 40 years". We used "since 1981". Confirm.
Is the estimate free? We say "written estimate" only. Is there an email address for quotes?
Office hours (MapQuest lists Mon to Sat 7 am to 6 pm; the site lists none).
Financing: offered, and through whom? Nothing is claimed.
Certifications to verify before we claim any: Brava (the site says "certified installer"), DaVinci, GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, Malarkey, IKO. We claim none.
BBB: the site says "A plus"; unverified, not used.
License and registration numbers (Kansas registration, Attorney General roofing registration) and insurance. None is shown.
Warranty terms in writing: workmanship 5, 10 and 15 years (which jobs get which), and manufacturer warranties.
Subcontractors: one 1-star review says a subcontractor did a roof, while the site says no commissioned salespeople. Does the crew include subcontractors?
Flat and EPDM roofs: the commercial page lists an EPDM job and one review says flat roofs are not their expertise. Do they want flat roofs offered?
Commercial: only four project names on the site. Which commercial work do they want to promote?
Names of the two lead foremen, and Jason's title (the owner reviews call him the business manager).
Legal name "Douglas Fry Roofing, Inc.": the pages use "Douglas Fry Roofing". Which should lead?
Service area: confirm Hays and Great Bend (named on the site) and how far they will travel.
Who receives the homepage form submissions, and does it work?
The three testimonials on the old site (Amber Snavely, Tony Martinez, Steve Lebeda): where from, and may we use them?
Logo file, brand colors and real job photos for the build.
